title: GracefulSoftStop preemption: tenant credit ledger + KV warmness heuristics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a GracefulSoftStop preemption mode that combines a tenant credit ledger with KV "warmness" heuristics to minimize quality regressions and KV churn during continuous batching preemption. This ticket designs and implements: (1) a per-tenant refundable credit ledger used to purchase protected micro-slices and enable soft-stop/resume semantics; (2) a KV warmness estimator (hotness + temporal locality) incorporated into eviction scoring; (3) a preemption flow that drains small remaining token budgets into a short soft-stop grace window to preserve KV residency and avoid cold restarts; and (4) GPU memory compaction and selective slab pinning to improve KV locality under constrained memory.
acceptance_criteria: Credit ledger records per-tenant spend and refundable credits visible in runtime metrics and Console
Soft-stop window (configurable) allows requests with <= X tokens remaining to be resumed without KV cold misses in >= 80% of cases in our synthetic workload
Eviction scoring that includes KV warmness reduces measured KV miss-rate by >= 25% for bursty tenant workloads versus baseline LRU under same memory pressure
End-to-end latencies for P1 tenants remain within configured SLO 95th percentile during preemption-induced scheduling events in production canaries
No new OOMs observed in dedicated canary cluster for a 72 hour stress run with simulated tenant mix
Feature flag gated rollout with metrics dashboard and automated rollback criteria in place
decisions: Use a lightweight on-node ledger (in-memory with optional CRDT-backed persistence) to keep preemption fast and avoid centralized contention
Implement warmness as a composite score: recency_decay * access_frequency * size_penalty, normalized per-model-family
Soft-stop window default 300ms or up to 64 tokens remaining (configurable), chosen to balance KV residency preservation vs head-of-line latency for high-priority tenants
Refund model: if a soft-stopped slice resumes within grace_window, most credits are refunded; long-term evictions consume credits permanently
GPU slab pinning will be conservative: only pin top-N KV entries per-tenant by warmness_score and only when free memory < threshold
implementation_notes: Ledger: API surface to create/spend/refund/query credits (proto + REST). Ledger entries include tenant_id, slice_id, credit_delta, reason
Scheduler: integrate ledger check during admission; if credits available, attempt soft-stop reservation for in-flight slices
KV estimator: maintain per-entry metadata: last_access_ts, hit_count, byte_size. Compute warmness via exp_decay on last_access and frequency bucketization
Eviction: combine warmness_score with global memory pressure signal and tenant priority weight to compute eviction_rank
Memory compaction: implement async kernel to defragment GPU slabs at low-utilization; run compaction only if fragmentation metric > 30%
Metrics: ledger.balance, ledger.spend_rate, kv.warmness_histogram, kv.miss_rate, scheduler.soft_stop_events, scheduler.resumed_within_grace
Instrumentation: add trace spans for preemption path (preempt.request -> ledger.check -> softstop.reserve -> kvpin/evict -> resume)
Config: expose per-tenant soft_stop_policy (disabled | conservative | aggressive) and global defaults in Console
testing_plan: Unit tests: ledger invariants (spend/refund), warmness estimator math, eviction ranking determinism
Simulator: extend continuous-batching simulator to run mixed-tenant workloads with bursty short requests and long context sessions to measure KV miss-rate and resume success
Canary: staged rollout to 5% of runtime fleet, run 48-hour stress test with production-like tenant mix
Chaos test: inject sudden memory pressure and node restarts to validate refunds and ledger reconciliation
Perf benchmarks: measure 95p latency and cost-per-token under preemption vs baseline over identical load
rollout_plan: Feature-flag behind runtime flag 'graceful_softstop_v1' initially off
Internal alpha: enable for internal tenants + dev orgs for 1 week
Beta: enable for low-volume external tenants (opt-in) for 2 weeks while collecting metrics
Canary: enable for 5% of production nodes for 48 hours; evaluate rollback criteria
Ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% over 4 weeks contingent on metrics
Rollback: automatic rollback if kv.miss_rate increases by > 15% or P1-tenant 95p latency regresses by > 12%
